questions.question: Which of the following natural resources is classified as a non-renewable resource?
questions.explanation: Non-renewable resources exist in fixed amounts and cannot be regenerated by natural processes on human timescales. Examples include mineral ores, crude oil, and coal, whereas water, geothermal energy, and solar radiation are renewable resources.

questions.question: Which drainage system in Ethiopia covers the largest catchment area and contributes approximately 60% of the country's total annual water discharge?
questions.explanation: The Western (Mediterranean Sea) drainage system—comprising the Abbay, Tekezze, and Baro-Akobo river basins—is the largest drainage system in Ethiopia, discharging about 60% of the country's total annual water volume into the Nile River system.

questions.question: What is the deepest natural lake in Ethiopia, reaching a maximum depth of 266 meters?
questions.explanation: Lake Shalla, located in the Main Ethiopian Rift, is the deepest lake in Ethiopia with a maximum recorded depth of 266 meters.

questions.question: Which major soil type in Ethiopia, also known as Red Basaltic soil, is deeply weathered, friable, rich in iron and aluminum, and represents the most widely cultivated soil for coffee, enset, and cereals?
questions.explanation: Nitosols (Red Basaltic soils) cover about 12% of Ethiopia. They are deeply weathered, friable, well-drained, and rich in iron and aluminum oxides, making them the most agriculturally productive and widely cultivated soils in the highlands.

questions.question: Which endemic mammal of Ethiopia is strictly native to the Semein Highlands and is classified as a wild goat threatened by extinction?
questions.explanation: The Walia Ibex is an endemic wild goat species found exclusively in the rugged Afroalpine cliffs of the Semein Mountains in northern Ethiopia.

questions.question: Which river in Ethiopia is unique in that it is the only river in the country used for inland water navigation?
questions.explanation: The Baro River in Gambella is the only navigable river in Ethiopia because it flows across a flat lowland plain with a gentle gradient and maintains a sufficient volume of water during wet periods.

questions.question: Why does the Wabe Shebelle River, despite being the longest river inside Ethiopia (1,340 km), fail to reach the Indian Ocean directly?

options.text: It terminates in Lake Abbe on the border with Djibouti.
It flows into Lake Turkana along the Kenyan border.
It dries up and disappears in the sand dunes near the Benadir coast of Somalia.
It joins the Baro River to flow into the Nile River system.

questions.explanation: Although the Wabe Shebelle is the longest river within Ethiopian territory, its flow diminishes as it crosses the arid southeastern lowlands, ultimately drying up in the coastal sand dunes and swamps of Benadir in Somalia before reaching the Indian Ocean.

questions.question: What physical property makes Vertisols (Black Basaltic soils) difficult for farmers to till during the peak rainy season?

options.text: Their high gravel and coarse sand content which causes severe tool abrasion.
Their high clay content, which makes them extremely sticky when wet and prone to waterlogging.
Their high salt accumulation (salinity) which burns crop roots.
Their shallow soil profile over unweathered granite rock.

questions.explanation: Vertisols contain a high percentage of expanding clay minerals. When wet, they swell, become extremely sticky, and experience poor drainage and waterlogging, making tillage difficult without specialized land management.

questions.question: In which region of Ethiopia are the primary active gold mining operations of Lega Dembi and Sakaro located?

options.text: Adola / Shakiso area in Southern Oromia

questions.explanation: Lega Dembi and Sakaro are major primary gold mining sites located in the Precambrian rock belt of Adola / Shakiso in southern Oromia.

questions.question: Which plant species are recognized as the dominant vegetation indicators in the Afroalpine and Sub-Afroalpine altitudinal zones (above 3,000 meters) of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: In the cold high-altitude Afroalpine and Sub-Afroalpine environments above 3,000 m.a.m.s.l. (such as the Bale and Semein mountains), Gibra (giant lobelia) and Asta (Erica/heather) are the characteristic dominant vegetation species.

questions.question: How does the origin of Lake Tana differ from that of Lake Shalla and Lake Abaya?

options.text: Lake Tana is a crater lake formed by a volcanic explosion, whereas Lake Shalla is a man-made reservoir.
Lake Tana is a watershed lake formed when a sheet of flowing lava dammed a surface depression, whereas Lake Shalla and Lake Abaya are tectonic Rift Valley lakes.
Lake Tana was formed by glacial erosion during the Quaternary period, whereas Lake Shalla was formed by river deposition.
Lake Tana is an alkaline salt lake, whereas Lake Shalla is a freshwater highland lake.

questions.explanation: Lake Tana is a highland watershed lake formed during the Quaternary period when a lava flow dammed a shallow depression between the Gojjam and Gondar massifs. In contrast, Lakes Shalla and Abaya were formed by tectonic faulting on the Rift Valley floor.

questions.question: Fluvisols cover about 10% of Ethiopia's total surface area. Which combination of origin, location, and agricultural potential correctly describes Fluvisols?

options.text: They are weathered basaltic soils found on steep mountain slopes with low fertility.
They are transported alluvial soils deposited along lower river valleys and lake basins, possessing very high agricultural potential.
They are ancient metamorphic soils in arid lowlands with high salinity and low organic content.
They are young lava-derived soils restricted to the Rift Valley floor used exclusively for nomadic pastoralism.

questions.explanation: Fluvisols are alluvial soils formed from fine sediments deposited by rivers in lower valleys and floodplains (e.g., lower Awash, Omo, Baro, Abbay). Because they are continuously enriched by flood-borne nutrients, they possess excellent agricultural potential.

questions.question: How does the Awash River Basin structurally differ from the Abbay, Baro-Akobo, and Genale River Basins in terms of its course and final destination?

options.text: Awash is an international transboundary river flowing to the Atlantic Ocean, while the others flow to the Red Sea.
Awash originates in the Rift Valley and flows into Lake Victoria, while the others drain into local crater lakes.

Awash is an internal river system that originates on the Shewan Plateau, flows through the Rift Valley, and terminates in Lake Abbe without crossing an international border, whereas the others flow across international boundaries.
Awash has no major tributaries, whereas the others receive water only from glacier meltwater.

questions.explanation: The Awash River belongs to the Inland (Rift Valley) Drainage System. It originates on the Shewan Plateau, flows along the Great Rift Valley, and ends inside Lake Abbe on the Djibouti border, unlike the transboundary river basins (Abbay, Baro-Akobo, Genale) that leave Ethiopian territory.

questions.question: Which pair of non-metallic minerals found in the Rift Valley and Afar Depression of Ethiopia provides essential raw materials for the domestic chemical industries of soda ash and fertilizer manufacturing, respectively?

options.text: Sodium Carbonate / Soda Ash (Lakes Abijata & Shalla) and Potash / Salt (Dallol / Danakil Depression)

questions.explanation: Rift Valley lakes such as Abijata and Shalla contain massive brine reserves of sodium carbonate used for soda ash production, while the Dallol Depression in Afar contains vast potash and salt deposits suitable for commercial fertilizer and chemical production.

questions.question: Which of the following options correctly matches the endemic Ethiopian mammal with its specific primary geographic habitat?

options.text: Mountain Nyala → Semein Mountains; Walia Ibex → Bale Mountains
Swayne's Hartebeest → Nechsar National Park & Sankalle Sanctuary; Semien Fox → Bale & Semein Highlands
Gelada Baboon → Ogaden Lowlands; Wild Ass → Kafa Rainforests
Menelik's Bushbuck → Danakil Depression; Walia Ibex → Baro Lowlands

questions.explanation: Swayne's Hartebeest is protected in Nechsar National Park and Sankalle Sanctuary, while the Semien Fox (Ethiopian Wolf) inhabits the Afroalpine highlands of Bale and Semein. (Option A is incorrect because Mountain Nyala is native to Bale and Walia Ibex to Semein).
